editorial:
Imagine a world where a few powerful people can ruin millions of lives just to make a buck. You get to follow three different people whose lives are all connected by the opioid crisis. There is a drug dealer moving Fentanyl across the border, a mom trying to save her son from addiction, and a professor who finds out his boss is lying about a new drug. It feels like a high-stakes game of chess where everyone is trying to stay one step ahead of the law or their own secrets. The vibe is tense and serious, making you feel the pressure these characters are under as their worlds slowly crash into each other.

The acting is top-notch and keeps you glued to the screen, though the plot moves very quickly and can be a bit confusing at first. You will love how the different storylines finally click together, even if some parts feel a little too dramatic. If you enjoy crime stories that feel like they could actually happen in real life, you should definitely check this out. It looks great in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but you might want to grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture quality possible.
endingExplained: Everything comes together when you realize the drug company and the traffickers are working toward the same goal. The professor exposes the company's lies about their new painkiller, proving it is actually addictive. Meanwhile, the drug dealer's plan to flood the market is revealed. The movie ends by showing that while some individuals get caught, the big system of greed and corruption usually keeps running, leaving you feeling a bit uneasy about the real world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves conspiracy thrillers and gritty crime dramas.
